html:
The championship of men's national football teams in Africa, first played in Khartoum in February 1957. It is organised by the Confederation of African Football, founded the same year.

Only three teams took part in the first tournament: Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia. South Africa was to be the fourth, but it would only send an all-white team, so it was excluded. Under apartheid it stayed out of African football until 1992; it hosted and won the cup in 1996. Egypt won the first title and has won the most since.

The tournament grew as independent nations joined, and it is now usually held every two years with 24 teams. It is the biggest sporting event on the continent, followed by vast television audiences, and a stage for national pride. African teams also became a force at the World Cup, which Africa hosted for the first time in the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa.
sum: The championship of men's national football teams in Africa, first played in Khartoum in February 1957. It is organised by the Confederation of African Football, founded the same year.
